craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as remembered-entered-known; vyabhicāri peace of conduct remembered (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: smaranti…viśanti…viduḥ (REMEMBER…ENTER…KNOW — the ascent order kept); punaḥ punar (AGAIN and AGAIN — doubled, kept doubled); nigamana (the hymn names its own close — seal-effect). Rows: 9 (‘again and again’ anchor), 6 (self-naming close kept as anchor — ‘ultimate discourse’ verbatim, never reworded), 12 (śānta-fall: ‘three worlds’ — wide, still, long vowels close the whole work). Close: ‘the three worlds’. Rupture: ‘And they’ (conduct turns to persons — the remembered becomes the rememberers). Rejected: ‘often’ — killed: repetition IS the practice; reordering to close on ‘known’ — killed: remembered→entered→known is the ascent. Read aloud: THIS-SEVEN-fold GOOD-con-DUCT … RIGHT-ly re-MEM-ber … EN-ter the su-PREME a-BODE a-GAIN and a-GAIN … DIS-course OF the THREE-worlds.

lines: This sevenfold good conduct — those whose other thoughts have melted, who long for the ultimate, rightly remember in the heart.
And they — O Bhairava’s own — enter the supreme abode again and again, and know the ultimate discourse of the three worlds.
l4.sanskrit_cite: sadvṛttasaptakam idaṃ galitānyacintāḥ samyak smaranti hṛdaye paramārthakāmāḥ | te bhairavīya paradhāma muhur viśanti jānanti ca trijagatīparamārthacarcām

reads_against.argmap: The conduct-septad remembered in the heart; the abode entered again; the discussion itself known — the hymn names its own close. → Remembered, entered, known — the hymn closes by naming itself.
c1_essence: The conduct-septad remembered in the heart; the abode entered again; the discussion itself known — it names its own close.
